actions.name: approve_invitation
actions.description: Accepts a pending LinkedIn connection invitation, which immediately makes the sender a 1st-degree connection and notifies them. This changes state on the user's account, so the user must explicitly approve it before you call it; get all inputs from list_invitations, read immediately beforehand.

invitation_id.description: Identifier of the pending invitation to accept, taken from the list_invitations result.

validation_token.description: Single-use validation token for this invitation, taken from a list_invitations call made immediately beforehand; it cannot be reused.

profile_id.description: Identifier of the profile of the person who sent the invitation, taken from the same list_invitations result.

_payload.value: ["Sorry, invitation from Jai not accepted. Please try again."]

actions.name: create_post
actions.description: Publishes a text-only post to the user's LinkedIn feed. This changes state on the user's account and creates a real, public post visible to anyone immediately, so the user must approve it before you call this tool. It cannot attach images, video, links, polls, or @mentions/hashtags, and it returns the new post's URN (urn:li:ugcPost:...).

actions.name: get_company
actions.description: Fetch a LinkedIn company page by its universalName (the slug in linkedin.com/company/<universalName>), returning compact rows for the company plus related organisations such as affiliates and similar pages, with fields like company_urn, name, universal_name, url, tagline, description, employee counts, website, and industry_urn. Read-only and safe to retry; match the returned universal_name against the one requested to identify the target company.

universal_name.description: The company's universalName slug from its LinkedIn page URL (linkedin.com/company/<universalName>), e.g. "microsoft".

actions.name: get_me
actions.description: Identifies the signed-in LinkedIn member, returning their own profile_urn (the mailbox_urn that list_conversations and send_message require), member_urn, first_name, last_name, public_identifier (the /in/ slug), occupation, and premium status. Call this first for any messaging task; it is read-only, takes no parameters, and is safe to retry.

actions.name: get_profile
actions.description: Resolves a LinkedIn public profile vanity name (the '/in/<name>' slug) to the member's profile URN (strip 'urn:li:fsd_profile:' to get the ACoAA… id needed by list_followers), name, headline, premium flag, summary, country code, location and industry URN. An empty result means the slug did not resolve (renamed or private), never a different person. Read-only and safe to retry.

vanity_name.description: The public identifier from the profile URL's '/in/<name>' path, without slashes or domain, e.g. 'williamhgates'.

actions.name: get_profile_education
actions.description: Fetches a LinkedIn member's education history as one row per entry (school_name, degree_name, field_of_study, start_year, end_year, description), most recent first as LinkedIn returns them. This is a read-only operation with no side effects and is safe to retry.

vanity_name.description: The member's LinkedIn vanity name, i.e. the slug after /in/ in their profile URL (for example, "williamhgates"). Same identifier used by get_profile.

actions.name: get_profile_experience
actions.description: Fetch a LinkedIn member's work history as one row per position (title, company, company_urn, location, start/end year and month, description), most recent first; a row with no end_year is a current role. Read-only and safe to retry.

vanity_name.description: The member's LinkedIn vanity name, i.e. the slug after /in/ in their profile URL (e.g. "williamhgates"), the same identifier get_profile takes.

actions.name: list_conversations
actions.description: List the LinkedIn member's most recent ~20 message threads (inbox), newest first, with conversation_urn, unread counts, participants and the latest message preview; use it as the entry point for reading or replying to messages. This is read-only and safe to retry; for older threads or name/keyword lookups use search_conversations or the paging tools.

actions.name: list_invitations
actions.description: Lists the member's pending received LinkedIn connection invitations, returning one row per invitation with invitation_id, validation_token, invitation_type (GenericInvitationType_CONNECTION for a person, GenericInvitationType_ORGANIZATION for a company page, which has no profile_id) and profile_id for person invites. This is read-only and safe to retry; call it immediately before approve_invitation or reject_invitation, since both the id and the single-use token are required and old tokens should not be reused.

actions.name: list_mailboxes
actions.description: Lists the LinkedIn company-page mailboxes the signed-in member administers, returning one row per page mailbox with mailbox_urn (urn:li:fsd_pageMailbox:<id>), company_urn (the owning urn:li:fsd_company:<id>) and messaging_enabled. It excludes the member's personal inbox, and a pageMailbox urn cannot be used as the urn:li:fsd_profile:… that send_message expects. Read-only, cheap, and safe to retry.

actions.name: list_people_at_company
actions.description: Lists people who work at a given LinkedIn company, paginated at 12 per page by default, returning one row per person with name, headline, location, profile_url, profile_urn, degree (DISTANCE_1/2/3, OUT_OF_NETWORK, SELF) and total (the full result set size, repeated on every row). This is a read-only operation with no side effects and is safe to retry; to filter by name or role within the company, use search_people_at_company instead.

actions.name: list_shared_connections
actions.description: Lists LinkedIn mutual connections (people who are 1st-degree connections of both you and another member) for a given profile, 10 per page, with name, headline, location, public profile URL, profile_urn and degree. Read-only and safe to retry; results are capped at 1000 rows and limited to your network reach, and this differs from list_followers or the member's full connection list.

actions.name: reject_invitation
actions.description: Declines a pending LinkedIn connection invitation by sending the same ignore action as the UI's dismiss button, removing it from the member's pending list without notifying the sender. This changes state on the user's LinkedIn account immediately and cannot be undone, so the user must approve it before you call it; call list_invitations right before to obtain fresh inputs.

invitation_id.description: ID of the pending invitation to decline, taken from the list_invitations result you just read.

validation_token.description: Single-use validation token for this invitation, from the list_invitations result read immediately beforehand. Re-list invitations to get a new one if it has been used or is stale.

profile_id.description: LinkedIn profile ID of the invitation's sender, as returned by list_invitations for that invitation.

_payload.value: ["Sorry, invitation from Jai not ignored. Please try again."]

actions.name: search_companies
actions.description: Search LinkedIn for companies by name or keyword, returning 10 results per page with name, industry, city, follower count, company page URL, and numeric company id. Use it to resolve a company name to the universal_name slug that get_company needs. Read-only and safe to retry.

keywords.description: Company name or keyword to search for, e.g. "Microsoft".

actions.name: search_companies_and_people
actions.description: Read-only, safe-to-retry LinkedIn typeahead that returns a few quick people, company, and search-phrase suggestions for a typed query. Use it to resolve a company name to its numeric company id (strip 'urn:li:company:' from tracking_urn) for people/job search tools; it does not return the universalName slug that get_company needs (use search_companies for that) and is not for full result sets.

actions.name: search_jobs_at_company
actions.description: Lists open LinkedIn job postings at a given company within a required country or city geography, returning 10 postings per page with title, job_urn, reposted flag and the total count of open postings (location and description are not included). Read-only and safe to retry.

company_id.description: LinkedIn numeric company ID, obtained from search_companies_and_people or search_companies (e.g. 1035).

geo_id.description: Required LinkedIn geography ID for a country or city (e.g. 103644278 = United States, 101165590 = United Kingdom). There is no worldwide option; an omitted or unsupported value silently falls back to the member's own country.

actions.name: search_people
actions.description: Search all of LinkedIn for people by free-text keywords using the full search-results page (not the 4-row typeahead). Returns 10 results per page with name, headline, location, profile URL, profile_urn and connection degree (DISTANCE_1/2/3, OUT_OF_NETWORK, SELF); pass a result's profile_urn to list_followers, or use search_people_at_company to search within one company. Read-only and safe to retry.

keywords.description: Free-text search terms, such as a person's name, job title or employer (e.g. "Satya Nadella").

actions.name: search_people_at_company
actions.description: Search LinkedIn for people at a specific company using a company filter plus free-text keyword matching over names and headlines. Returns 12 people per page (name, headline, location, profile_url, profile_urn, degree, total), paged with `start`. This is read-only and safe to retry.

company_id.description: LinkedIn numeric company ID to search within, e.g. "1035". Obtain it from search_companies_and_people or search_companies.

keywords.description: Free-text query matched against people's names and headlines, e.g. "engineer".

actions.name: send_connection_request
actions.description: Sends a LinkedIn connection invitation (without a note) to another member. This changes state on the user's account: the recipient is notified immediately and it counts against the weekly invite quota, so the user must approve it before you call it. Returns the new invitation urn; to respond to invitations received, use list_invitations with approve_invitation or reject_invitation instead.

profile_urn.description: The recipient's LinkedIn profile urn, obtained from search_people_at_company. Identifies who receives the invitation.

member_id.description: The recipient's LinkedIn member ID, if available from the profile data. Optional supporting identifier.

first_name.description: The recipient's first name, as shown on their profile. Optional.

last_name.description: The recipient's last name, as shown on their profile. Optional.

vanity_name.description: The recipient's public profile vanity name (the custom part of their LinkedIn URL). Optional.

profile_picture_payload.description: The recipient's profile picture data as returned with their profile details. Optional; pass through unchanged if available.

actions.name: send_message
actions.description: Sends a real LinkedIn message into an existing conversation thread on the user's account; the recipient receives it immediately and it cannot be unsent. This changes account state, so the user must approve it before you call it. It cannot start a new thread, and it returns the created message's URN and echoed body.

text.description: The body of the message to send, exactly as the recipient should see it.

conversation_urn.description: URN of the existing conversation thread to send the message into. A new thread cannot be created with this action.
